direct_observation: legal integrity provisions are established while supplier integrity, targeted tools and digital risk management remain underdeveloped
evidence_status: high for policy-to-practice signal; public-good receipt remains open

direct_observation: procurement is about 13% of OECD GDP; risks occur pre-tender, tender and post-award; red flags include single bids and contract changes
evidence_status: high for risk architecture; flags have multiple causes and are not proof
next_test: investigate flagged and unflagged contracts with market and place context

source_title: OECD citizen trust and public-value evidence
direct_observation: integrity failures can increase price, reduce quality and delay services; few countries measure trust effects
evidence_status: medium-to-high for consequence framing; citizen attribution remains open
next_test: measure named resident service receipt, quality, burden and trust after delivery

direct_observation: transparency, competition, objective criteria, records and challenge mechanisms underpin procurement; reforms include e-procurement and tender publication
evidence_status: high for international standard; implementation varies by sector and country
next_test: follow one reviewed reform into award, challenge, delivery and remedy

direct_observation: winning bidders disclose beneficial owners in applicable procurements and information is published in award notices
evidence_status: high for disclosure route; prevention, collusion and delivery effects remain open
next_test: match ownership data to bids, subcontracting, red flags, delivery and enforcement

source_title: OECD/World Bank corruption-collusion and red-flag evidence
direct_observation: corruption and collusion can reinforce each other; red flags can also reflect thin markets, geography or capacity
evidence_status: high for uncertainty boundary; causal wrongdoing and public outcome require case closure
next_test: triangulate red flags with market structure, investigation, service result and recurrence
